more_info.overview: Lactitol is a disaccharide alcohol manufactured by catalytic hydrogenation of lactose, with anhydrous and hydrated crystalline forms. It provides sweetness when added to the food or used in a table-top sweetener preparation. Made by catalytic hydrogenation of lactose. Its starting material is the milk sugar lactose. The specified material is supplied as colourless powder or crystalline material. The specification identifies water solubility as one of its properties.
more_info.origin: Made by catalytic hydrogenation of lactose. Its starting material is the milk sugar lactose.
more_info.dietary_restrictions: The specified manufacturing process uses lactose. The specification does not identify the commercial lactose feedstock, so vegan and religious suitability cannot be established from it alone.
more_info.uses:
Examples in the EU food-use list include certain cocoa and Chocolate products as covered by Directive 2000/36/EC; other confectionery including breath freshening microsweets; chewing gum; decorations, coatings and fillings, except fruit-based fillings covered by category 4.2.4; fruit juices as defined by Directive 2001/112/EC and vegetable juices; flavoured fermented milk products including heat-treated products.
The entries apply to particular food categories and may limit the amount, the preparation or the way it is used; they do not show how often the additive appears in retail products.
